claims.text: Approximately 1 wt.% oxygen significantly reduces lattice thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr through enhanced defect-induced phonon scattering.
Oxygen-induced phonon scattering markedly decouples lattice heat transport from electronic heat transport.
Below 200 K, the electronic and lattice contributions to thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
Above 300 K, approximately 1 wt.% oxygen lowers lattice thermal conductivity by more than 30% relative to pristine HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed model will predict total thermal conductivity within ±15% of experimental observations.
HfNbTaTiZr possesses inherent atomic-scale chemical disorder.
Monte Carlo sampling can generate statistically representative configurations that capture both intrinsic high-entropy disorder and oxygen-defect distributions.
Atomic-scale disorder, local chemical fluctuations, and oxygen impurities modify phonon dispersion and phonon scattering rates.
Computing separate electron and phonon scattering rates with the proposed framework will decouple the two heat-transport channels.
Oxygen impurities enhance phonon scattering at high temperatures.
Electronic heat conduction remains relatively invariant when approximately 1 wt.% oxygen is added.
Explicit treatment of disorder and separate transport channels will improve predictive accuracy relative to perfect-crystal simulations.
Measured total thermal conductivity for the oxygen-containing alloy is 10–17 W/(K m).
Previous analytical and DFT-based estimates assumed defect-free, perfect crystals.
Previous analytical and DFT-based estimates conflated electron and phonon contributions.
The assumptions in previous approaches caused larger prediction errors and prevented them from capturing distinct temperature-dependent behavior.
The proposed approach is valid for HfNbTaTiZr and similar refractory high-entropy alloys containing up to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen over 200–1200 K.
The approach may not be applicable outside 200–1200 K or at substantially different oxygen concentrations.

contradictions.description: The stated applicability range begins at 200 K, but the hypothesis predicts behavior below 200 K and requires below-200 K validation for falsification. Those low-temperature claims therefore fall outside the declared model boundary.
